usage.outputShape: body.exists (bool), body.rules[] ({user_agent, allow[], disallow[]}), body.sitemaps[], body.user_agents[], body.blocks_all_crawlers, body.total_rules; if no robots.txt: body.exists=false + body.message. Payment/meta in body._meta.
quirks: The `url` is a query-string parameter, not a JSON body — it's a GET request. Pass the target site root or robots.txt URL as ?url=.
If the target site has no robots.txt, the call still succeeds (200, paid) and returns {exists:false, message:'No robots.txt found.'} — pick a site you know has robots.txt to see full rule parsing.
Price is dynamic ('Varies' on the registry surface); observed $0.0216 USDC on Base for example.com.
usage.guide: Call GET https://api.strale.io/x402/robots-txt-parse with a single query parameter `url` set to the target domain (e.g. https://example.com); the service appends/parses that site's robots.txt. Pay via x402 (~$0.0216 USDC on Base, price varies). The JSON response is plain synchronous: read body.exists to confirm a robots.txt was found, then body.rules[] for per-user-agent allow/disallow directives, body.sitemaps[] for declared sitemaps, and body.blocks_all_crawlers as a quick gate. If exists is false the call still succeeds and charges — use a domain known to have robots.txt for real data.
